title: Set a gel tray up to cast: crosswise so its end gaskets seal, comb in an end slot
instruction: Set the gel box up to cast a gel. Put the gel tray on the grey platform in the tank turned crosswise, so its two open ends, which carry the black gaskets, face the tank's two side walls and are sealed by them (not toward the electrodes). Then stand the comb in the comb slot nearest one end of the tray, across the tray with its bar down in the notches of both side walls. Let go of both.
context: Biological and laboratory technicians (O*NET 19-4021.00, 29-2012.00) cast agarose gels every day for DNA and RNA electrophoresis. In gasket-type horizontal gel boxes the gel is cast in the tank itself: the UV-clear tray, open at both ends, is turned crosswise on the platform so the rubber gaskets on its open ends press against the tank's side walls and seal them, and the comb is stood in the slot near one end, so the wells sit at one end of the gel with its whole length to run. Once the gel has set, the tray is turned lengthwise to run it. A tray left lengthwise leaks the molten agarose out of both open ends; a comb in the middle slot halves the run length (that slot is for a second row of wells). Here the tray starts lengthwise on the bench, so it has to be turned a quarter turn on the way in, and the comb has to go into the right slot.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything except the gel tray and the comb is fixed to the table. (1) Gel tank: an open-top box of clear acrylic (rendered pale blue-grey), outside 106 mm (x) by 240 mm (y), 45 mm tall, walls 6 mm thick, floor 4 mm thick, centred at x 32.0 cm, y 0. Its two side walls run along y, their inner faces at x 27.3 and 36.7 cm, 94 mm apart; its end walls' inner faces are at y +11.4 and -11.4 cm. (2) Casting platform: a grey acrylic block 94 mm (x, the tank's full inner width) by 110 mm (y), 12 mm tall, on the tank's floor at its centre (y -5.5 to +5.5 cm); its top is 16 mm above the table. (3) Electrodes: two plastic bars standing in for the platinum wires, 80 mm (x) by 4 by 4 mm, on the tank's floor centred at x 32.0 cm: black (cathode) at y -10.0 cm, red (anode) at y +10.0 cm, so a gel runs along y. (4) Gel tray, loose, 38 g: a rigid UV-clear acrylic tray (rendered pale grey), 84 mm long from gasket face to gasket face, 64 mm wide and 18 mm tall: an 80 x 64 x 4 mm floor, two 80 mm side walls along its length, 5 mm thick and 18 mm tall, and two open ends, each with a black rubber gasket strip 2 mm thick, 64 mm wide and 14 mm tall across the floor's end. Each side wall has three notches in its top, 22 mm wide and 5 mm deep, facing the other wall's: the comb slots, one at the middle of the tray's length and one 25 mm either side of it (their centres 17 mm in from the gasket faces). It lies on the table open side up and lengthwise (its length along y), centred at x 18.0 cm, y +27.0 cm. (5) Comb, loose, 20 g: black acrylic, a bar 72 mm long, 12 mm thick and 18 mm tall with its teeth under the middle of the bar (one plate 44 mm wide, 3 mm thick and 7 mm deep stands in for the teeth). Seated in a slot, the bar's two ends rest in the facing notches of both side walls (4 mm of bar past each wall) and the teeth end 2 mm above the tray's floor. (6) Comb stand: two white plastic plates, each 5 mm (x) by 50 mm (y), 18 mm tall, 6 mm apart, centred at x 18.0 cm, y -27.0 cm. The comb stands in it with its bar along y across both plates' tops and its teeth in the gap; the bar's ends stick out 11 mm past the plates. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the tray's and the comb's poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a top photo and a steel rule). 'Set to cast': the tray lies open side up on the platform, tilted 3 degrees or less, every corner of its underside within 2 mm of the platform's top height and over the platform (within 55 mm of y 0); it is crosswise, its length within 12 degrees of x (the line between the side walls); and each gasketed end's face is within 10 mm of the side wall it faces (the 94 mm gap leaves 10 mm of play in all, so this means down between the walls). Between the walls the tray can turn at most about 10 degrees from crosswise; turned lengthwise it fits on the platform too. 'Seated' in a slot: the comb upright (within 5 degrees of the tray's vertical, teeth down), its bar within 10 degrees of the tray's width, its middle within 6 mm of the tray's centre line (teeth between the side walls), and at both side walls the bar's underside within 1.5 mm of the notch bottoms (13 mm above the tray's underside) and within 6 mm of the same slot's centre along the tray. 'At rest': no corner of the tray's underside (for the comb, neither end of its bar) moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. 'Clear' of a part: each gripper's fingers at least 20 mm from it (a gripper's fingers are taken as everything within reach of a pad's outer corner around the 38 mm stretch back from the point between its pad tips: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across, up to 57 mm when fully open). Score 0 if the tray is not set to cast, not at rest, or a gripper is not clear of it (still holding the tray, or holding the comb in it), whatever the comb does: lengthwise (gaskets toward the electrodes), on the bench, propped on a wall top, upside down, held. Otherwise: 1.0 if the comb is seated in one of the two end slots (either end), at rest, both grippers clear of it; 0.75 if seated so in the middle slot; 0.5 otherwise (the comb not seated so: in its stand, held, on the bench, lying in the tray, resting on the side walls' tops, or in a slot but still moving or with a gripper within 20 mm of it). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (success, held 1 s); every outcome maps to one of them.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The tank is fixed blocks with no lid, buffer, leads or power; the electrodes are coloured bars. The gaskets are rigid strips, so the tray sits between the side walls with 5 mm of play at each end where real rubber gaskets are squeezed against them. No agarose is poured. The comb's teeth are one 3 mm plate, and its slots leave 5 mm of play a side. The scorer reads the parts' poses and the grippers' positions and openings, not forces.
reset_notes: Put the gel tray back on the table open side up and lengthwise (its length along y), centred at x 18.0 cm, y +27.0 cm, and stand the comb back in its stand with its bar along y and its teeth in the gap between the plates. Nothing is consumed; the tank, platform, electrodes and stand are fixed.
